title.full: Checking a number you reported by mistake

summary.text: Check whether the number is marked as scam. If it was wrongly marked, call 1799 to request an unblock.

details.heading: One report is not enough
details.body: A single report alone does not automatically mark a number as scam. If the number is legitimate, it will not be incorrectly marked based on a single report.

steps.name: Check the number
steps.text: Use Check for Scams to see whether the number is marked as scam. A red result says it looks like a scam; an unsure result means it has not been marked as scam or blocked.

items: Use Check for Scams to see whether the number is marked as scam.
A red result says, “Beware, this looks like a scam.”
An unsure result means the number has not been marked as scam or blocked.

about.text: A number is only blocked when the result is red with the message “Beware, this looks like a scam.”

steps.name: Request an unblock
steps.text: If you believe the number has been wrongly marked as scam, call the ScamShield Helpline at 1799 to request an unblock.

items: If you believe the number has been wrongly marked as scam, call the ScamShield Helpline at 1799 to request an unblock.

sources.page_title: What should I do if I accidentally reported a number as scam?

quotes.text: If you believe a phone number has been wrongly marked as scam, please reach out to the ScamShield Helpline at 1799 to request an unblock.
If you've accidentally reported a number as "scam", you may use the Check for Scams feature to check if the phone number is marked as scam in the ScamShield database.
A phone number is only blocked if the check outcome appears red with the message "Beware, this looks like a scam."

Please be assured that a single report alone does not automatically mark a phone number as a scam. Our system uses multiple data points and verification processes to determine if a number is suspicious.
